skill.name: lark-markdown
skill.description: Manage native Markdown files in Lark Drive by creating, fetching, comparing, patching, and overwriting content through lark-cli.
skill.summary: Create, retrieve, compare, and update native Markdown files in Lark Drive.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Six path findings are confirmed because the skill mandates loading sibling instructions outside the audited package. Other static detections are documentation syntax, placeholder URLs, or plain Markdown, while two medium data-integrity and permission risks were found semantically.

remediation.issue: The skill requires agents to read lark-shared instructions outside the audited package.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the required rules inside this skill or include the sibling dependency in the same audited artifact.

remediation.issue: The patch workflow can overwrite a concurrent remote update.
remediation.suggestion: Add optimistic version checks and stop for user review when the remote version changes before upload.

remediation.issue: Bot-created files can trigger an automatic full-access grant to the current CLI user.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit permission confirmation and offer a least-privilege role before granting full access.

semantic_findings.title: Non-Atomic Patch Can Lose Concurrent Updates
semantic_findings.description: The patch workflow downloads, edits, and overwrites the whole file without a version guard. A concurrent remote edit can be silently replaced.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference explicitly states that patch is non-atomic and can overwrite changes made between download and upload.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Full-Access Permission Grant
semantic_findings.description: Creating a file as a bot can automatically grant the current CLI user full access. This ACL change may exceed a creation-only request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference directly documents an automatic full_access grant after bot-based creation and describes its permission result.

content.value_statement: Managing native Markdown across Lark Drive and local drafts requires several precise commands. This skill guides safe creation, retrieval, comparison, patching, and replacement.
actual_capabilities: Creates native Markdown files in a Lark Drive folder or Wiki node.
Fetches remote Markdown content and can save it to a local path.
Compares two remote versions or a remote version with a local draft.
Applies one literal or RE2 regular expression replacement to a remote file.
Overwrites remote Markdown using inline content, a local file, or standard input.
Supports user and bot identities when the available permissions allow them.
limitations: It handles native Markdown files, not imported Lark docx documents.
It does not manage search, permissions, comments, moves, renames, or deletion.
Patch supports one replacement group and is not an atomic remote update.
It requires lark-cli, valid authentication, and access to the target Drive resource.

use_cases.title: Publish Project Notes
use_cases.description: Create a native Markdown file from a local project note and place it in the correct Drive folder.

use_cases.title: Review Documentation Changes
use_cases.description: Compare a remote Markdown version with a local draft before replacing shared documentation.

use_cases.title: Update Repeated Content
use_cases.description: Apply a controlled literal or regular expression replacement across one remote Markdown file.

prompt_templates.title: Read a Remote File
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the Lark Markdown file with token {file_token}. Return its content without saving a local copy.

prompt_templates.title: Create from a Local Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a native Markdown file from {local_file} in Drive folder {folder_token}. Preview the request before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Before Publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare remote file {file_token} at version {version} with {local_file}. Summarize additions and deletions without changing either file.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Regular Expression Patch
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview one RE2 patch on {file_token}. Replace {pattern} with {replacement}, explain escaping, and do not upload until I confirm.

output_examples.input: Fetch the remote README and show its content.
output_examples.output: The README was retrieved successfully. It contains the project overview, installation steps, and contribution guidelines.

output_examples.input: Compare the latest remote file with my local draft.
output_examples.output: The files differ. The local draft adds three lines, removes two lines, and changes one installation step.

output_examples.input: Replace the old release label and preview the update.
output_examples.output: The preview found one match. The final file remains nonempty, and no remote version was uploaded.

best_practices: Use dry-run before create, overwrite, or regular expression patch operations.
Prefer user identity for files owned in a user's cloud space.
Compare the latest remote version before overwriting shared content.
anti_patterns: Do not guess whether a token belongs to a Drive folder or Wiki node.
Do not use an unescaped regular expression for literal punctuation.
Do not treat patch as atomic when other users may edit the file.

faq.question: Can this skill create a Lark online document?
faq.answer: No. It creates native Markdown files stored in Drive, not imported docx documents.

faq.question: Can it save a remote file locally?
faq.answer: Yes. Fetch accepts a local output file or directory and protects existing files unless overwrite is enabled.

faq.question: Can it compare two historical versions?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the file token and version identifiers obtained from Lark Drive version history.

faq.question: Does patch change only one server-side section?
faq.answer: No. It downloads the complete file, replaces matching text locally, and uploads the complete result.

faq.question: Can one patch apply several different replacements?
faq.answer: No. Each patch supports one pattern and one replacement value.

faq.question: Which identity should I use?
faq.answer: Use user identity for personal cloud resources. Use bot identity only when the application has the required access.
